item.title: Blockchain-Based Regulatory Computing Framework for Privacy-Preserving Data Sharing Among Intelligent Vehicles
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · Ming Li, Haolun Huang, Yuhui Su
In the field of intelligent vehicles, collecting data to optimize the user experience often raises regulation and privacy issues, hindering effective data utilization. This paper presents a blockchain-based regulatory computing framework for privacy-preserving data sharing among intelligent vehicles. First, a federated learning environment is established on the basis of blockchain. This environment effectively addresses regulation issues and provides an infrastructure for the responsible use of intelligent vehicle data. A secure aggregation method is then introduced on the basis of grouped Shamir secret sharing. This method addresses the critical issue of privacy data leakage, ensuring that user data are well protected during sharing. Moreover, we explore incentive mechanisms and weight distribution strategies. The incentive mechanism aims to encourage active collaboration among participants, and the weight distribution strategy ensures optimal results during the training process and supports sustainable development. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system, we conduct a series of experiments using different datasets. The results show that our mechanism performs exceptionally well in terms of key performance indicators such as performance, latency, and training effectiveness while also providing sufficient data protection. This study offers a reliable method of regulation and privacy protection for intelligent vehicle data.

item.title: DeepSanitizer: Data-free Backdoor Removal in Deep Neural Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing · Yiming Wu, Nanjie Yao, Chong Long Fu, Chenghui Shi, Tiejun Wu, Shouling Ji
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are widely utilized in various Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, such as face recognition, speech assistant, and autonomous driving. However, recent studies reveal DNN's vulnerability to backdoor attacks, also known as trojan attacks. A backdoored DNN makes wrong predictions when the input contains the trigger, which poses significant security threats to DNN-based AI systems. Existing backdoor removal methods often require access to clean validation samples or samples with the trigger. However, this may not be feasible in some real-world scenarios, such as when dealing with models from online platforms or federated learning environments. To bridge this critical gap, we propose DeepSanitizer, which introduces a new algorithmic formulation for data-free backdoor mitigation. Unlike prior detection-focused workFreeEagle, DeepSanitizer shifts the paradigm directly to backdoor removal. Rather than merely applying known reverseengineering techniques to reconstruct triggers or integrating existing pruning models into a pipeline, DeepSanitizer synthesizes benign dummy representations to fine-tune the compromised model classifier. This enables the mitigation of diverse backdoor attacks without the need for access to either clean or poisoned data. Specifically, our method splits a compromised model into two components: the feature extractor and the model classifier via an introduced inspection layer. Then it utilizes a novel gradient-based algorithm to generate feature representations as the dummy data for fine-tuning the model classifier to remove the backdoor. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach effectively removes planted backdoors while maintaining the model performance, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art data-free and non-data-free backdoor mitigation techniques. Finally, DeepSanitizer reduces the defense time to just minutes, greatly faster than the existing methods.

item.title: Transmit Coefficients and Receive Combining Vector Design for OTA-FL With Imperfect CSI
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Xiaoyan Ma, Shahryar Zehtabi, Yinan Zou, Taejoon Kim, Christopher G. Brinton
Over-the-air (OTA) computation has recently gained significant attentions as an effective approach to enhance the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning (FL). By enabling simultaneous transmission and aggregation of local model updates, OTA-FL can substantially reduce both latency and bandwidth consumption. However, a key challenge lies in the imperfect aggregation of global models caused by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, which introduces distortion to the final learning performance. To address this issue, we study the long-term mean squared error (MSE) minimization problem for OTA-FL under imperfect CSI conditions. Through convergence analysis, we establish an upper bound for the time-averaged MSE, thereby revealing the effect of aggregation errors accumulated throughout multiple communication rounds on the overall training performances. Based on this analysis, an optimization framework is developed to minimize the long-term MSE via the joint design of (i) transmit coefficients at the local devices and (ii) receive combining vectors at the parameter server (PS). Since this alternating optimization approach requires non-causal CSI, a Lyapunov-based optimization method is further introduced to handle causal CSI scenarios. By incorporating virtual queues to characterize long-term energy consumption, the proposed method effectively decouples temporal dependencies and allows transmit coefficients to be optimized based on the causal CSI of each aggregation round. Comprehensive evaluations on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the degradation of test accuracy caused by imperfect CSI. Comparisons with other benchmark schemes further verify the superiority of our proposed algorithms.

item.title: Beyond Personalization: Federated Recommendation With Calibration Via Low-Rank Decomposition
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering · Jundong Chen, Honglei Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Chunxu Zhang, Zhiwei Li, Yidong Li
Federated recommendation (FR) is a promising paradigm to protect user privacy in recommender systems. Distinct from general federated scenarios, FR inherently needs to preserve client-specific parameters,i.e., user embeddings, for privacy and personalization. However, we empirically find that globally aggregated item embeddings can induce skew in user embeddings, resulting in suboptimal performance. To this end, we theoretically analyze theuser embedding skewissue and proposePersonalizedFederated recommendation withCalibration viaLow-Rank decomposition (PFedCLR). Specifically, PFedCLR introduces an integrated dual-function mechanism, implemented with a buffer matrix, to jointly calibrate local user embedding and personalize global item embeddings. To ensure efficiency, we employ a low-rank decomposition of the buffer matrix to reduce the model overhead. Furthermore, for privacy, we train and upload the local model before personalization, preventing the server from accessing sensitive information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PFedCLR effectively mitigates user embedding skew and achieves a desirable trade-off among performance, efficiency, and privacy, outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.

item.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Networking · Yang Jiao, Kai Yang, Jianwei Huang
Multi-level learning/optimization, e.g., bilevel optimization, has been recognized for its versatile applicability across a broad array of domains, spanning from signal processing to machine learning. However, most existing works focus on bilevel and trilevel optimization. In contrast, multi-level optimization problems involving four or more hierarchical levels, which we term poly-level learning (PLL) problems, remain largely unexplored.In addition, in practical PLL, data may be distributed across multiple nodes over a distributed network. Nevertheless, extant studies on PLL predominantly focus on the non-federated setting, necessitating the collection of data to central servers and thereby posing potential privacy risks. To this end, we propose a Federated Poly-Level Learning (FPLL) framework over a distributed network to tackle the PLL problems with soft constraints in a federated manner. FPLL hinges on a novel non-linear cut, i.e., $L$-cut, for the level-wise relaxation to the PLL problems. Additionally, the proposed federated algorithm is designed with adjustable parameters that allow for a flexible trade-off between its computational complexity and performance efficiency, enabling users to tune it according to specific application requirements. We also carry out non-asymptotic analysis to derive the iteration complexity for the proposed FPLL to achieve the $ε$-Pareto stationary point. Extensive experiments have been undertaken to elucidate the superior efficacy of the proposed method.

item.title: Adaptive Beam Hopping and Power Control for Dual-Layer Over-the-Air Online Federated Learning in LEO Satellite Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Communications · Zhendong Li, Shaojie Wang, Zhou Su, Zihao Zhang, Haixia Peng, Nan Cheng
This paper investigates over-the-air (OTA) computation enabled online federated learning (FL) in low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Specifically, we consider a dual-layer OTA aggregation architecture, where ground devices upload analog model updates to serving satellites via uplink OTA aggregation, and satellites forward the aggregated signals to a data processing center through the second round OTA aggregation. Then, we formulate a long-term data-utilization maximization problem in which devices continuously collect new data and untrained samples gradually lose freshness. The problem is subject to the satellite beam budget, transmit-power limit, and global mean squared error (MSE) constraint that governs end-to-end aggregation distortion. This yields a coupled mixedinteger nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, involving tightly coupled discrete beam-hopping decisions and continuous power control. Due to the combinatorial action space and non-convex constraints, the problem is NP-hard and computationally intractable. Furthermore, the time-varying satellite topology and dynamic data generation render it a sequential decision-making problem, necessitating adaptive online scheduling. To address these issues, we cast the problem as a Markov decision process and develop a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes adaptive beam hopping and power control, using an MSE-aware reward to balance data utilization and aggregation accuracy. Numerical simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms other benchmark schemes, achieving superior long-term data utilization and faster FL convergence while satisfying the MSE requirement.

item.title: FedLoc-Guard: Cross-Round Behavior Modeling for Backdoor Defense in Federated RSSI Fingerprint Localization
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management · Xuejun Zhang, Hui Chen, Yexin Fan, Yanchun Hu, Jiami Guo, Xiaodong Yang
Federated learning provides a privacy-preserving paradigm for Wi-Fi RSSI fingerprint-based indoor localization, but remains vulnerable to stealthy backdoor attacks. In federated RSSI localization, environmental variation, device heterogeneity, and sampling-condition differences cause benign client updates to fluctuate across communication rounds, complicating malicious-update discrimination based on single-round statistics. To address this challenge, we propose FedLoc-Guard, a server-side defense framework that models client reliability from server-observable behavior across rounds. FedLoc-Guard estimates instantaneous reliability from directional consistency, relative update magnitude, and normalized turnaround-time consistency, updates client reliability across rounds, and uses the resulting reliability states for high-reliability client retention and risk-constrained aggregation with pre-normalization weight clipping. The method requires neither previously trusted clients nor an additional clean server-side reference set. Experiments on UJIIndoorLoc and Mall under IID and non-IID settings demonstrate that FedLoc-Guard substantially reduces attack success rates against BadNets, Scaling Attack, DBA, and an A3FL-inspired adaptive backdoor attack while maintaining useful localization performance under the evaluated settings, thereby improving the reliability and trustworthiness of federated indoor localization services.

item.title: Adaptive Quantization and Device Scheduling for Asynchronous Federated Learning Over Resource-Constrained Wireless Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Xiaodong Li, Yulong Gao, Fengyu Liang, Carla Fabiana Chiasserini
Federated learning (FL) is a promising distributed learning paradigm that enables multiple devices to collaboratively train a global model without sharing local private data. Considering the device heterogeneity in computation and communication capabilities, asynchronous aggregation is introduced in FL to improve the learning efficiency. However, asynchronous FL suffers from communication bottlenecks due to limited wireless resources. To address this issue, we propose AQAFL, an adaptive quantization method for asynchronous FL, while also integrating device scheduling and wireless resource allocation. We first present a convergence analysis of asynchronous FL with quantized transmission, and then formulate an optimization problem to minimize the convergence upper bound under long-term latency and bandwidth constraints by jointly optimizing the quantization bit width, device scheduling, and wireless bandwidth allocation. Following that, we analytically characterize the optimal bandwidth allocation and prove that it can be obtained via bisection search, and derive the closed-form expression for the quantization bit width. Subsequently, an efficient device scheduling strategy is proposed to determine the number of participating devices in each round. Experiments show that compared with other methods, AQAFL reduces the total communication overhead by up to 69% and the overhead required to achieve the same target test accuracy by 32.6%–88.6%, while improving test accuracy by 4.1%–6.5%.

item.title: DecFLDiff: Decentralized Semi-Supervised Federated Learning for Vehicular Networks Based on Diffusion Model
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Computing · Dacheng He, Weidi Wen, Yuxiang Chen, Junguo Liao, Wei Liang, Kuanching Li
The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) faces severe challenges, including high vehicle mobility, network instability, and massive sensitive data. While centralized federated learning (FL) offers privacy protection, it suffers from limited vehicle computing power and high data redundancy. To solve these issues, we propose DecFLDiff, an edge-assisted decentralized semi-supervised federated learning framework enhanced by a conditional diffusion model. In DecFLDiff, the semi-supervised classifier is trained offline at the edge server and deployed to vehicles in inference-only mode for pseudo-label generation, reducing the need for local vehicle training and making intelligent transportation systems more efficient and reliable in data-driven decision-making. Uploaded feature embeddings are perturbed with Gaussian noise before transmission, which helps preserve local distribution cues while reducing reconstruction risk. By implementing an adaptive hybrid topology, DecFLDiff flexibly adjusts to node density to balance information propagation speed and communication overhead among neighboring nodes and reduce redundant transmissions. By shifting computation-intensive learning and synthetic-data generation to resource-rich edge servers and reducing unnecessary peer-to-peer communication, DecFLDiff improves the overall computational and communication efficiency of decentralized learning in resource-constrained IoV environments. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 show that DecFLDiff outperforms representative decentralized federated-learning baselines under low-label regimes, boosting accuracy by 4%–17% and achieving faster convergence in terms of communication rounds in the reported experimental settings.

item.title: SecureFedIPM: Resilient and Privacy-Preserving Federated Intelligent Paging for 6G Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing · Cong Li, Xinsheng Ji, Weizhi Meng
Paging is a fundamental component of Next Generation Mobile Communication Systems (6G, NGMCS), enabling the support of the Internet of Everything (IoE) and ultra-reliable low-latency communications (uRLLC). However, existing paging mechanisms cannot simultaneously satisfy the requirements of paging efficiency, privacy preservation, and service resilience in the distributed architecture of 6G networks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Resilient and Privacy-Preserving Federated Intelligent Paging Mechanism (SecureFedIPM). First, SecureFedIPM builds upon our previous intelligent trajectory-prediction foundation to predict user equipment (UE) trajectories and optimize paging areas, while extending the paging formulation with resilience-aware constraints under node failures and external availability attacks. Based on the hierarchical federated paging architecture, a Hierarchical Privacy-Preserving Paging Architecture (HPPP) is further developed to support distributed collaborative learning while strengthening privacy protection through model-update clipping and differential privacy. Furthermore, a Dynamic Resilience Strategy (DRS) is integrated into HPPP to mitigate performance degradation under node failures and external availability attacks through adaptive aggregation and rapid recovery mechanisms. Experimental results on a real-world telecom dataset demonstrate that, under normal operating conditions ($F=0$), SecureFedIPM reduces paging signaling resources by 74.1% and paging delay by 35.6%. Under node failures and external availability attacks, SecureFedIPM degrades more slowly than the compared intelligent paging schemes, demonstrating its ability to maintain paging services under adverse conditions.

item.title: AFIND+ : Adaptive Client-Centric Collaboration for Decentralized Personalized Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Zhichao Wang, Lin Wang, Yongxin Guo, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang, Xiaoying Tang
Decentralized personalized federated learning (DPFL) enables devices to exchange knowledge over peer-to-peer links while retaining client-specific models. Its effectiveness, however, can be impaired by heterogeneous data: indiscriminate neighbor aggregation may introduce negative transfer. This work studies how a client can form a useful collaboration set under this heterogeneity. We proposeAFIND+(Adaptive, Filtered, and Intelligent Neighbor Discovery and Aggregation), a three-stage framework that (i) ranks candidate neighbors using a lightweight proxy of their update representation, (ii) adaptively filters the candidates through a confidence-dependent acceptance threshold, and (iii) aggregates the retained models with loss-based Boltzmann weights. The three stages serve complementary purposes: the first seeks low-discrepancy collaborators, the second controls the participation level, and the third distinguishes contributions within the selected set. Under smoothness and explicit stochastic and collaboration-error conditions, we establish a non-asymptotic bound for average personalized first-order stationarity, separating proxy/coreset, threshold-selection, aggregation, and local-update errors. Experiments on heterogeneous image and text benchmarks show improved accuracy and fewer rounds to a target accuracy relative to the evaluated DPFL baselines.AFIND+is designed as a communication-and-aggregation module that can be combined with personalized learning backbones.

item.title: Disentanglement-Guided Multi-Teacher Relational Distillation for Federated Class-Incremental Facial Expression Recognition
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Image Processing · Leying Jiang, Hu Ding, Chuhang Ke, Yan Yan, Rui Zhu, Hanzi Wang
Conventional facial expression recognition (FER) methods often train the model on large-scale centralized expression data. However, expression data are often distributed across heterogeneous devices and incrementally collected in practice. In this paper, we study a little-studied yet important task named federated class-incremental FER (FCI-FER), which aims to incrementally identify unseen compound expressions with the model initially trained on easily accessible basic expressions under the federated learning settings. To address the unique problems of catastrophic forgetting and heterogeneous disturbances across clients in FCI-FER, we propose a disentanglement-guided multi-teacher relational distillation (DMT-RD) method which follows a novel "distillation and disentanglement" paradigm. For local training, we design a multi-teacher hypergraph relational distillation (MTD) module to capture semantic relations between expressions and learn expression features. Meanwhile, we develop a disturbance encoding (DE) module to learn client-specific disturbance information. By minimizing the mutual information (MI) loss between the outputs of the MTD and DE modules, we can achieve feature disentanglement and reduce the negative influence of specific disturbances on local training. For global training, we introduce a multi-teacher learning strategy by clustering historical clients to comprehensively capture client diversity across communication rounds. Our method can effectively preserve old knowledge while learning new compound expressions under federated settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method against several state-of-the-art federated class-incremental learning methods on benchmark datasets.

item.title: SemFedVAE: A Communication-Efficient Federated Learning Framework for Variational Autoencoder With Semantic Latent Space Alignment
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Jincheng Cai, Qinglin Zhao, Jian Li, Li Feng, Xu Chen, Jian Zhu
Federated training of variational autoencoders (VAEs) must share distributional knowledge across clients without centralizing data or repeatedly exchanging high-dimensional model parameters. Under non-IID data, full-parameter federated optimization is communication-heavy, and clients can learn incompatible latent spaces that slow convergence and degrade reconstruction and generation. We propose SemFedVAE, a communication-efficient, personalized federated VAE framework in which clients keep their own encoders and decoders and share only latent posterior statistics. The server aggregates the semantic means and standard deviations, combining scales in the log-variance domain, into a global latent target. A global consistency (GC) term in the evidence lower bound (ELBO) aligns each local latent distribution with this target by minimizing their KL divergence. We analyze the communication complexity and show that, for bounded GC weights, the regularizer preserves the standard non-convex convergence order. Experiments on six datasets with 5–20 clients show that SemFedVAE reduces the per-round training payload by four to five orders of magnitude relative to full-parameter protocols that train a shareable global model, while remaining competitive in reconstruction and generation quality; a client without local data instead requires a one-time model transfer. Ablations compare the aggregation rule with variance-based alternatives and examine the GC strength and the label-aware extension.

item.title: BlockFormer: Towards Memory-Efficient Federated Learning Via Assembling Pre-Trained Blocks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Shichen Zhan, Hui Chen, Zichen Xu, Xiaobo Zhou, Li Li
Federated Learning (FL) enables multiple devices to collaboratively train a shared model for downstream tasks while preserving data privacy. However, the substantial memory footprint during the local training process hinders resource-limited devices from participating, thereby significantly degrading model performance. This paper introducesBlockFormer, an innovative FL framework designed to overcome memory constraints, enhancing both model performance and training efficiency. Rather than training the shared model from scratch, BlockFormer constructs the global model by assembling pre-trained neural network blocks, tailored to the data distributed across participating clients in order to deliver better memory and computing efficiency. Specifically, BlockFormer features three core components: 1) Client Grouper, 2) Adapter Configurator, and 3) Inference Accelerator. On the server side, the Client Grouper is designed to handle data heterogeneity in FL by clustering clients based on data distribution and strategically selecting participants in each round to enhance data diversity during training. On the client side, the Adapter Configurator ensures network blocks with different structures can be concatenated without sacrificing performance by designing tailored adapters based on their structural and dimensional differences. Moreover, the Inference Accelerator is deployed to reduce the additional computational overhead and latency introduced by block assembling, enhancing overall inference efficiency. It consists of two modules: the Model Fusioner optimizes multi-model inference introduced by block selection at the computation graph level through merging highly correlated computation nodes; the Resource Scheduler optimizes GPU execution by dynamically adjusting scheduling strategies based on task dependencies, ensuring efficient resource utilization and minimizing execution bottlenecks. Extensive experiments on representative datasets and edge devices demonstrate that compared to existing approaches, BlockFormer improves the model accuracy by up to 33.88%, achieves up to 17.94× speedup, and significantly reduces the memory footprint by up to 91% during the learning procedure.

item.title: FASAFL: Fairness Aware Starlink Assisted Federated Learning for Communication Heterogeneous Edge Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Yuncan Tang, Lina Ni, Jinquan Zhang, Yongquan Liang
Federated learning over heterogeneous edge net works is often limited by persistent communication imbalance. Devices with weak terrestrial connectivity may repeatedly miss upload deadlines and become underrepresented in global training. Existing terrestrial scheduling methods can improve resource utilization, but they still operate within the available ground network and cannot always recover devices whose terrestrial links remain infeasible. Satellite assisted federated learning provides wider communication coverage, but existing studies mainly focus on satellite resource coordination, hierarchical aggregation, or data offloading. They provide limited support for selectively using satellite access to recover long term participation of communication constrained ground devices. To address this problem, we propose FASAFL, a fairness aware Starlink assisted federated learning framework. FASAFL explicitly models Starlink as a dynamic and resource constrained uplink by incorporating satellite visibility, shared beam capacity, handover, gateway routing, weather conditions, and retransmission reliability into the access decision. The server selectively assigns Starlink to devices whose terrestrial links restrict timely participation, rather than treating satellite access as a uniformly better communication option. FASAFL further integrates learning value, resource expenditure, and participation history into the scheduling process, so that current satellite allocation is jointly coordinated with the long term participation of communication constrained devices. The server also uses bounded quality aware compensation during scheduling and aggregation to increase the opportunities of persistently underrepresented devices without giving excessive influence to stale or low quality updates. Experiments on four datasets with Hypatia and ns-3 based dynamic LEO simulations show that FASAFL improves effective participation, learning performance, fairness, and deadline reliability under limited satellite resources.

item.title: Federated Fractional Gradient Descent With Adaptive Parameter Updates for Accelerated Convergence on Heterogeneous Data
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics · Md Palash Uddin, Yong Xiang, Mahmudul Hasan, Kuo-Hui Yeh, Jine Tang, Yushu Zhang
Federated learning (FL) is a prominent machine learning (ML) framework that enables training a global model across distributed client devices without exposing their private data. However, traditional FL methods often face challenges in achieving fast convergence, particularly in heterogeneous or non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data environments. These issues arise primarily from inaccurate gradient estimation during the optimization process. To address these limitations, this article introduces an adaptive optimizer, federated fractional gradient descent with adaptive parameter updates (FedFGD-APUs). In particular, the proposed FedFGD-APU optimizer leverages fractional-order derivatives for efficient gradient computation. It employs an adaptive strategy to dynamically adjust fractional order, learning rate, and momentum to improve learning convergence and stability. We also develop a theoretical computational framework linking federated optimization with adaptive fractional derivatives, establishing the convergence of FedFGD-APU for nonconvex optimization settings with a convergence rate of $\mathcal {O}(1/T)$ . We conduct comprehensive experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and NSL-KDD datasets to validate FedFGD-APU's effectiveness under both IID and non-IID data distributions. The experimental results demonstrate that FedFGD-APU significantly improves communication speedups and testing accuracy across heterogeneous data scenarios.

item.title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning-Driven Secure Replication and Multiobjective Resource Optimization Framework for Edge Computing
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing · Zhou Zhou, Youbin Dong, Jemal Abawajy, Yifu Zeng, Yin Hui
In edge computing, data Replication Coding (RC) represents the overarching redundancy management paradigm for guaranteeing data availability and reliability, while Erasure Coding (EC) constitutes a more storage-efficient redundancy mechanism for implementing this paradigm. To bridge the gap where conventional EC and RC schemes prioritize fault tolerance at the expense of data privacy and model integrity, we propose a Federated Learning-driven failure prediction mechanism. By enabling edge nodes to perform localized training on sensitive data coupled with secure aggregation, our framework constructs a robust global model. This approach achieves collaborative forecasting of regional failures and workload dynamics while strictly maintaining data residency and mitigating the risks of model poisoning and adversarial propagation. Leveraging these predictive insights, we propose HRS, a Security-Aware Hybrid Replication mechanism that dynamically switches between EC and RC modes. HRS incorporates a quantitative security model centered on Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA), employing a cross-domain replica dispersion strategy to mitigate systemic risks from coordinated attacks and large-scale outages. To prevent security-related overheads from compromising system longevity, we further introduce the EMRA module, which utilizes Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) for residual energy forecasting and formulates a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to achieve a Pareto-optimal allocation across energy, latency, and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that HRS-EMRA maintains data residency and enhances resilience against poisoning and DDoS attacks, while achieving more than 90% data availability and a 13.2% 23.9% reduction in energy consumption. With end-to-end latency capped at 74.32 ms, our framework validates its efficacy in harmonizing privacy preservation, secure replication, and efficient resource orchestration.

item.title: Shard the Gradient, Scale the Model: Serverless Federated Aggregation via Gradient Partitioning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing · Amine Barrak
Federated learning (FL) aggregation on serverless platforms faces a hard scalability ceiling: existing architectures ($\lambda$-FL, LIFL) partitionclientsacross aggregators, but every aggregator must hold the complete model gradient in memory. When gradients exceed the per-function memory limit (e.g., 10 GB on AWS Lambda), aggregation becomes infeasible regardless of tree depth or branching factor. We propose GRADSSHARDING, which instead partitions thegradient tensorinto$M$shards, each averaged independently by a serverless function that receives contributions from all clients. Because FedAvg averaging is element-wise, this produces bit-identical results to tree-based approaches, so model accuracy is invariant by construction. Per-function memory is bounded at$\mathcal {O}(|\theta |/M)$, independent of client count, removing the per-function memory ceiling that limits full-gradient architectures. We evaluate GRADSSHARDING against$\lambda$-FL and LIFL through HPC experiments and real AWS Lambda deployments across model sizes from 43 MB to 5 GB. Results show a cost crossover at$\sim$500 MB gradient size, 2.7× cost reduction at VGG-16 scale, and that GRADSSHARDING is the only architecture that remains deployable beyond the serverless memory ceiling.

item.title: Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning with Heterogeneity-Aware Coordination Mechanism in Mobile Edge Computing Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Hushuang Zeng, Xiuhua Li, Guozeng Xu, Jinlong Hao, Xiaofei Wang, Victor C. M. Leung
Federated learning (FL) enables edge devices (EDs) in mobile edge computing (MEC) networks to collaboratively train a shared model without exchanging raw data. However, heterogeneous computing and communication capabilities, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, and limited wireless resources introduce straggler delays, stale updates, and client drift, thereby increasing convergence latency. To address these challenges, we propose SAFL-HACM, a semi-asynchronous FL framework with a heterogeneity-aware coordination mechanism for MEC networks. SAFL-HACM allows EDs to train independently and buffers their completed updates for selective aggregation without interrupting ongoing local training. It coordinates three components: 1) a local drift control mechanism that combines update-direction correction with a stateful drift variable to mitigate non-IID-induced drift and stale-model inconsistency; 2) a cluster-balanced scheduling strategy that jointly considers data-distribution representation, update staleness, local training utility, and participation history; and 3) a latency-aware bandwidth allocation scheme that minimizes the completion time of each aggregation cycle under a limited uplink bandwidth budget. Experiments across four benchmark datasets and different levels of data heterogeneity show that SAFL-HACM reduces convergence latency by 64.0% on average over representative baselines. Moreover, across different device scales, it improves test accuracy by an average of 6.5% while maintaining robust performance.

item.title: MDA: Tier and Availability-Aware Client Selection for Faster Cross-Device Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Reliability · Yunkai Bao, Hossein KhademSohi, Amin Eslami Abyane, Steve Drew, Hadi Hemmati
Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralising user data, but incross-devicesettings the large and volatile client population makes training slow and unreliable. Two factors dominate: (i) many devices are offline when polled, and (ii) the online devices differ widely in compute and network speed. We introduceTiFL–MDA, a composite client-selection strategy thatjointlytackles these hurdles. First,Tier-based FL (TiFL)groups clients into latency tiers that reflect their resource profiles; then theMust-Detect-Availability (MDA)filter chooses the most responsive clientswithin each tier. By coupling resource awareness and availability detection, TiFL–MDA maximises parallelism without sacrificing fairness. Across five datasets and six heterogeneity settings, TiFL–MDA reaches target accuracy in up to6.5 % fewer communication roundsthan vanilla FL and improves final accuracy by up to23 %. Unlike 'fast-only' selection, our tier-aware design prevents bias towards high-end devices.

item.title: FedAuto: An Adaptive Federated Learning Framework for Auto Insurance Claim Prediction
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics · Qing Han, Xuebin Ren, Shusen Yang, Jia Hu
Automobile insurance claim prediction require sufficient quality data from various data curators (e.g., insurance companies and telematics providers) to build effective models. However, the intermittent communication bandwidth, privacy and security issues are the main obstacles to the information sharing. The reliability and efficiency of data sharing need to be further enhanced. In this paper, we propose FedAuto, a sequential horizontal-vertical Federated Learning (FL) framework to relieve transmission load and address privacy concerns of data holding parties for claim prediction in automobile insurance industry. Differing from existing FL methods that only support single data partition mode, FedAuto constructs a tightly coupled end-to-end workflow for domain business requirements, can jointly handle horizontal and vertical data separations. In particular, we develop an adaptive differential privacy enhanced horizontal FL for multi-drivers’ collaborative behavior risk prediction and a clustering-optimized encrypted vertical FL for accurate claim prediction, together with an architectural interface for passing HFL-derived driving-risk features to VFL claim-cost modeling. Finally, extensive experiments on public datasets show that FedAuto achieves a 9.35× reduction in HFL readiness-collection time relative to synchronous baselines and a 18.11× reduction in the calculated VFL full-tree payload upper bound relative to SecureBoost.

item.title: Privacy-Enhanced Federated Learning With Dynamic Reputation Consensus for Smart Grids
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics · Zhuoqun Zhang, Haipeng Peng, Lixiang Li, Shuang Bao
Smart-grid services increasingly rely on distributed learning, but pooling regional load records, operating parameters, and topology information can violate privacy and critical-infrastructure constraints. Federated learning avoids direct data sharing, yet local updates remain exposed to gradient inversion, protected aggregation limits the observability of Byzantine poisoning and free-riding behavior, and static blockchain trust can be strategically manipulated. This article proposes privacy-enhanced federated learning with dynamic reputation consensus for secure smart-grid collaboration. Its protected update path combines integral affine-bijective grouped encoding, participant-specific masking, Paillier aggregation, and Shamir-based mask recovery to reduce encrypted payloads, retain a masking layer after private-key exposure when masks remain unavailable, and tolerate participant dropout. A benchmark-model-driven Euclidean distance and cosine similarity audit converts complementary magnitude and directional evidence into cross-round reputation for validator and leader selection and deposit-based incentives. Experiments on heterogeneous image benchmarks and two real-world load-forecasting tasks show stable utility under non-IID data, independent, mixed, and delayed strategic poisoning, and dropout rates up to 30%. In the evaluated LeNet-5 configuration, the encrypted payload decreases from 812.19 MiB for parameterwise Paillier-FedAvg to 7.96 MiB per client per round. Under the evaluated attack conditions, the key-exposure test yields distorted reconstructions. The election tests show close agreement between empirical and theoretical leader-election probabilities.

item.title: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Meta Learning for Personalized Edge Devices
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Ying Zhu, Yang Xu, Hongli Xu, Yunming Liao, Zhiwei Yao, Liusheng Huang
Recently, aided by edge computing (EC), federated meta-learning (FML) has been proposed to adequately utilize personalized data on different edge devices by incorporating meta-learning with federated learning (FL). Unlike conventional FL which conducts several stochastic gradient descent (SGD) steps to directly update the local model in each training round, FML first performs some SGDsteps to obtain a reference model and then performs a meta-step to update the local model along the direction towards the reference model. In this way, FML can identify common patterns and structures across different clients (i.e., edge devices) and quickly adapt to new data distributions, which exhibits its advantage in dealing with statistical heterogeneity inherent in FL. However, existing FML approaches struggle to effectively cope with two key challenges: i) the disparity in dataset informativeness among clients with statistically heterogeneous local data; and ii) the disparity in computing capacities among clients with heterogeneous hardware configurations. Herein, we propose a heterogeneity-aware FML framework, termed HFML, which explores adjusting the execution frequencies of SGD step and meta-step in each training round to address the above statistical and system heterogeneity challenges simultaneously. We introduce usable information (UI) as a new metric in HFML to quantify dataset informativeness, and theoretically analyze the influence of the execution frequencies of SGD steps and meta-steps on model performance and convergence speed. Based on the theoretical analysis, we develop an efficient optimization algorithm to jointly adjust the execution frequencies for different clients to handle the heterogeneity issues, which contributes to accelerating model training and enhancing personalization performance. Experimental results demonstrate that HFML can speed up training by up to 4.02× and improve model accuracy by an average of 11.5% compared to the baselines under heterogeneous settings.

item.title: Toward Model-Contrastive Federated Learning With Lightweight Privacy Preservation and Poisoning Attack Detection
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing · Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Guijuan Wang, Fenghua Xu, Yongzhao Zhang, Chunqiang Hu
Federated learning (FL), a distributed computing paradigm, is vulnerable to poisoning attacks that impair model performance and privacy attacks that leak participant information. Existing FL defense schemes struggle to counter poisoning attacks under data heterogeneity and high privacy computation overhead, limiting the practicality of federated learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a model-contrastive federated learning framework with lightweight privacy preservation and poisoning attack detection, named MCFL. Specifically, we design a novel model-contrastive term by aligning intermediate-layer representations of models in the local optimization function to promote consistency of model updates among benign participants. Additionally, we design a secure aggregation protocol that adopts two-server aggregation instead of the single server to resist poisoning attacks with lightweight privacy protection. The proposed MCFL is theoretically proven in terms of convergence, robustness, and privacy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of MCFL compared to existing FL defense schemes.

item.title: GPAFed: Gradient Projection-Guided Adaptive Aggregation Strategy for Federated Learning Under non-IID Data
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Xing Chang, Mohammad S. Obaidat, Xiaoping Xue, Jingxiao Ma
Under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data conditions, static weighted aggregation strategies in Federated Learning (FL) often fail to reflect each client's effective contribution to the global objective. This limitation may induce gradient conflicts, leading to unstable convergence and model performance degradation. To address this issue, we propose a Gradient Projection-guided Adaptive aggregation strategy for Federated Learning (GPAFed). We derive a novel convergence bound that explicitly incorporates the projection of local gradients onto the global gradient, revealing its quantitative influence on global loss reduction in FL. Building on this insight, we formulate a projection-based client contribution metric and design an adaptive aggregation weighting strategy inspired by the softmax mechanism. This approach strengthens the influence of high-contribution clients while attenuating the adverse effects of low-quality updates. Finally, we provide a theoretical guarantee that the proposed strategy achieves a tighter convergence bound. Extensive experiments under diverse non-IID conditions demonstrate that GPAFed consistently outperforms strong baselines in terms of model accuracy, convergence speed, and robustness.

item.title: Correcting Representation Bias in Latency-Selected Distributed Data Streams: A Federated Learning Perspective
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering · Yibo Chen, Zhizhong Liu, Yunchuan Qin, Zhuo Tang, Keqin Li
In distributed data stream processing, buffered asynchronous aggregation collects the first returned updates into a buffer and treats them as a representative sample of the population. Under non-IID data and system heterogeneity, this latency-selected stream can be temporally fresh yet statistically unrepresentative: fast client groups may dominate the buffer while slower groups carrying complementary population directions are systematically absent. We formalize this failure mode asdirection-level representation skewand propose DirBridge, a server-side stream-summary framework that corrects the bias without delaying aggregation or storing per-client entire caches. DirBridge compresses update directions with Count Sketch features, clusters clients into spherical direction groups, and refills only the missing group mass using exponential-moving-average (EMA) group memories. The abstraction is group-based rather than identity-based, reducing auxiliary server storage. We show that group-size-aware refill can eliminate the mixture-weight error under an ideal representative condition, and we further bound the residual convergence error. Experiments on vision, character recognition, and speech workloads under synthetic and natural latency traces show that DirBridge improves stream representativeness when direction skew is large, preserves accuracy when skew is low, and incurs modest overhead. These results position direction-group memory as a practical bias-correction abstraction for latency-selected distributed data streams.

item.title: Pull-in Aggregation Protocol: A Receiver-Oriented Decentralized Federated Learning Paradigm
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Fang Shi, JianKang Zeng, Shunpu Tang, Weiwei Lin, Qiong Huang, Li Shen
Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) trains models collaboratively without a central server, but asymmetric and time-varying communication often leads to imbalanced information flow and biased aggregation. Most existing methods address this issue with push-sum normalization, which requires maintaining auxiliary normalization states and can accumulate numerical drift, thereby slowing mixing and degrading convergence under limited connectivity. To address this, we propose Pull-in protocol, a receiver-driven decentralized learning frame work for directed time-varying graphs. Instead of relying on indiscriminate broadcasting, each receiver actively pulls models from a budgeted subset of incoming neighbors and constructs a row-stochastic aggregation vector locally. This receiver-side normalization makes the model aggregation step a stable convex combination by design and avoids push-sum-type normaliza tion variables in directed model mixing. To mitigate the bias caused by directed and asymmetric aggregation, we incorporate a gradient-tracking correction mechanism. In Pull-in-GT, the model aggregation matrix is row-stochastic, while the tracking matrix is constructed to be column-stochastic, enabling average preservation of the tracking variable over directed graphs. We establish convergence guarantees under standard smooth non convex objectives and bounded stochastic noise. The resulting bound explicitly separates optimization progress from consensus induced error terms and yields the rate O(T−1/2) quantifies the mixing speed of the induced row-stochastic matrix. Extensive experiments on vision-centric decentralized learning benchmarks demonstrate that Pull-in consistently improves training stability and achieves stronger performance than representative push-sum based DFL baselines across a wide range of network asymmetries.

item.title: Joint Route Scheduling and Adaptive Data Offloading for Federated Edge Learning in STIN
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Yatong Zhang, Weixiao Meng, Shuyi Chen
In Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks (STIN), distributed Federated Edge Learning (FEL) has become mainstream methods for data processing and analysis. The traditional FEL algorithm assigns devices for local training and satellites for aggregation to perform intelligent prediction and decision-making. However, it adopts a synchronous aggregation mechanism, where model updating is performed only after all devices complete training. Considering the heterogeneous computational frequency of devices and the advanced onboard processing capabilities of satellites, satellites act as participants in collaborative local training. In this paper, we introduce a Data Offloading-enabled Federated Edge Learning (DO-FEL) framework, where devices offload part of their data to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. The LEO satellites also act as Edge Servers (ESs), while the Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellite performs global aggregation. In DO-FEL, the dynamic satellite-device visibility and the limited computational frequency of a single satellite incur additional delay for FEL in STIN. Based on this, we propose a Dynamic Route Scheduling (DRS) strategy to optimize multisatellites' assistance for the collaborative training. Meanwhile, we propose an Adaptive Joint Delay-Energy Optimization (AJDEO) strategy. For different task requirements, the AJDEO strategy adjusts the devices' offloading proportion to balance overall delay and energy consumption. Experimental results show that with the DRS strategy, the DO-FEL framework reduces satelliteside delay and further reduces the overall delay. Besides, the proposed framework with two strategies achieves the trade-off between the overall delay and energy consumption compared with other baselines. This paper provides a new perspective for efficient FEL in STIN through flexible data offloading under actual satellite-device visibility.

item.title: Data-Scarce Intelligence of Machine Learning Approaches for Agricultural Transformation in the Congo: A Review
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on AgriFood Electronics · Eloge Wabanga Kasongo, Guangjie Chen
This article discusses the potential of machine learning (ML) to provide transformative benefits to agricultural development in traditionally data-scarce contexts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Data scarcity is characterized by low-quality, insufficient, or expensive information. In this study, we review a set of ML approaches that are particularly suited to low-resource environments to address these challenges, including transfer learning, few-shot learning, federated learning, synthetic data generation, and active learning (AL). The term “data-scarce intelligence” is defined as the strategic use of ML approaches for obtaining useful insights and enabling intelligent decision-making in environments with little, low-quality, or expensive data. Key Agriculture 4.0 use cases, such as crop yield prediction and plant disease detection, illustrate the significance of these approaches. While ML systems in data-rich contexts often report accuracy levels above 90%, the results discussed here suggest that more modest but still practical performance—typically between 70% and 85%—can be achieved in early-stage, data-limited deployments. However, major obstacles persist, including very low data levels, underdeveloped digital infrastructure, and a lack of local human technological capacity. The article concludes with a roadmap suggestion for effective implementation of ML, which can lead to sustainable changes in agricultural practice and food security in the region.

item.title: FedEL++: Efficient Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Clients
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Letian Zhang, Jieming Bian, Lei Wang, Jie Xu
Federated learning (FL) allows distributed devices to collaboratively train models while preserving data privacy, but heterogeneous computation and communication resources create stragglers, slowing training and limiting scalability. Existing methods, such as client selection, asynchronous FL, and partial training, partially address this but often reduce accuracy or disrupt model consistency. We propose FedEL++, a federated elastic learning framework that addresses both computation and communication heterogeneity. FedEL++ introduces a globally coordinated sliding window, anchored to the slowest client, and optimizes block window selection across all clients under a unified runtime constraint. Within each window, elastic tensor selection accounts for computation and communication costs, while a global-aware tensor importance adjustment mitigates model drift under non-iid data. Experiments on real edge devices and large-scale simulations show that FedEL++ achieves faster convergence, lower training time, and reduced memory and energy usage, while maintaining or improving model accuracy compared to existing FL methods.

item.title: FedTADA: Trajectory-Aware Displacement Aggregation for Sparse Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Xianyao You, Tingting Wu, Hao Zhang, Wei Zhang, Siyao Cheng, Jianxing Liu
Federated Learning in Internet-of-Things networks confronts a fundamental spatio-temporal trade-off driven by statistical heterogeneity and severe client participation sparsity. Traditional optimization frameworks struggle between two suboptimal extremes: instantaneous aggregation in Drop mode, which suffers from persistent sampling variance due to tiny active client subsets, and historical caching in Stale mode, which incurs cumulative spatial divergence and staleness bias from outdated local updates. In this paper, we proposeFederated Trajectory-Aware Displacement Aggregation (FedTADA), an optimization framework formulated in cumulative displacement space. To stabilize scale normalization without stochastic feedback loops,FedTADAintroduces a zero-order probing phase that establishes an exogenous energy reference anchor. Guided by an unnormalized negative entropy regularizer, we derive a scale-equivariant exponential controller that dynamically balances instantaneous descent against historical consensus. Theoretical analysis proves thatFedTADAachieves higher-order variance suppression, accelerating the client-sampling variance decay rate from the standard$\mathcal {O}(1/T)$down to$\mathcal {O}(1/T^{2})$via a joint Lyapunov potential function that strictly neutralizes staleness bias while isolating the irreducible Local-SGD drift floor. Extensive experiments across four distinct modalities under fully trainable end-to-end convolutional architectures demonstrate thatFedTADAachieves significant accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under extreme label skew with zero additional client-side computational or communication overhead.

item.title: FuzzyCS: Adaptive Client Selection via Fuzzy Rough Approximations in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence · Qianlong Dang, Baosheng Li, Binquan Guo, Qiqi Liu, HAN Shoufei, Guoqing Li
The client selection of federated learning presents a pivotal dilemma necessitating the harmonization of performance and efficiency. Prevailing studies frame this dilemma within the context of a multi-armed bandit optimization problem. With an expanding client base, the complexity of the task increases exponentially, demanding advanced algorithms to efficiently navigate the decision space. Fuzzy sets offer a clear depiction of the uncertainties associated with client selection, eliminating the need for intricate numerical computations. To this end, this paper proposes a fuzzy client selection (FuzzyCS) method. Specifically, we construct a fuzzy multi-criteria information matrix based on several selection criteria and use it to introduce a criteria-oriented fuzzy selection model. By leveraging the fuzzy rough approximations, we can estimate the fuzzy relationship between the criteria-oriented fuzzy concepts of each client and its likelihood of being selected. FuzzyCS can actively balance performance and efficiency by constructing an adaptive fuzzy approximation set, which incorporates the upper and lower approximate fuzzy rough sets. Experimental results demonstrate that FuzzyCS achieves the top Friedman rank in both performance and efficiency. The code is available athttps://github.com/dqlme/FuzzyCS.

item.title: Mitigating Instability and Knowledge Omission in Over-the-Air Federated Continual Learning
item.description: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Xiuheng Liao, Weiyu Wang, Tao Liu, Zhiwei Si, Dongrui Huang, Yong Yu

item.title: FLR-SS: Accelerating Federated Large Language Model LoRA Tuning by Structural Sparsification
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Xiaoxin Su, Yipeng Zhou, Lin Zhu, Quan Z. Sheng, Ennan Zhai, Laizhong Cui
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks; however, training them from scratch requires substantial computational resources. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as an efficient fine-tuning technique that enables the adaptation of pre-trained LLMs to specific tasks with significantly reduced computational cost. In Federated Learning (FL), mobile clients operate under constrained communication and computational resources, making LoRA particularly important for efficient model adaptation. However, directly applying LoRA in FL can still incur substantial communication overhead, particularly in wireless environments. To address this, we propose a novel framework, called Federated LoRA with Structural Sparsification (FLR-SS), which reduces communication cost by sparsifying LoRA matrices through the removal of rows and columns with the smallest norms, thereby preserving the most informative components. We further provide a theoretical convergence analysis of FLR SS and formulate the selection of rows and columns as a bi convex optimization problem, which can be solved efficiently. Extensive experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate that FLR-SS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving accuracy improvements of 1.66% to 8.63% while reducing communication traffic by 21.42% to 53.33%.

item.title: Decomposed Federated Transfer for Cross-Domain Recommendation: A Cluster-Tensor Perspective With Semantic Consistency Filtering
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering · Jianli Zhao, Qingqian Guan, Dianer Yu, Wei Wang, Jingwen Liu, Huan Huo
Cross-Domain Recommendation (CDR) effectively alleviates the data sparsity problem by transferring knowledge from source domains to target domains. To address growing data privacy concerns, Federated Learning (FL) has been incorporated into CDR, enabling multiple clients to collaborate without exposing raw data. However, most existing federated CDR methods still rely on overlapping entities to bridge different clients. Under strict privacy constraints, such correspondences are often unavailable, causing structural misalignment across isolated clients and weakening cross-domain knowledge transfer. To address this problem, we propose DFTCDR, aDecomposedFederatedTransfer framework forCross-DomainRecommendation. DFTCDR performs cluster-level structural alignment across disjoint domains through complementary modeling of transferable cluster-level structures and local residual interaction patterns. Specifically, we employ PARAFAC2-based tensor decomposition to learn transferable cluster-level structural prototypes, which act as virtual anchors for mapping isolated clients into a shared structural space. To balance transferability and personalization, DFTCDR further models local residual information through intra-domain graph propagation. In addition, a consistency-aware knowledge filtering mechanism evaluates whether each global prototype is consistent with the client local interaction semantics and retains only locally consistent prototypes to mitigate negative transfer. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that DFTCDR outperforms baselines without relying on overlapping entities. Additional experiments demonstrate its overall effectiveness and domain sparsity robustness.

item.title: DeFRiS: Silo-Cooperative IoT Applications Scheduling via Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Zhiyu Wang, Mohammad Goudarzi, Mingming Gong, Rajkumar Buyya
Next-generation Internet of Things (IoT) applications increasingly span across autonomous administrative entities, necessitating silo-cooperative scheduling to leverage diverse computational resources while preserving data privacy. However, realizing efficient cooperation faces significant challenges arising from infrastructure heterogeneity, Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) workload shifts, and the inherent risks of adversarial environments. Existing approaches, relying predominantly on centralized coordination or independent learning, fail to address the incompatibility of state-action spaces across heterogeneous silos and lack robustness against malicious attacks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DeFRiS, a Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning framework for robust and scalable Silo-cooperative IoT application scheduling. DeFRiS integrates three synergistic innovations: (i) an action-space-agnostic policy utilizing candidate resource scoring to enable seamless knowledge transfer across heterogeneous silos; (ii) a silo-optimized local learning mechanism combining Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) with clipped policy updates to resolve sparse delayed reward challenges; and (iii) a Dual-Track Non-IID robust decentralized aggregation protocol leveraging gradient fingerprints for similarity-aware knowledge transfer and anomaly detection, and gradient tracking for optimization momentum. Extensive experiments on a distributed testbed with 20 heterogeneous silos and realistic IoT workloads demonstrate that DeFRiS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, DeFRiS reduces average response time by 6.4% and energy consumption by 7.2% compared to the best-performing baseline, while lowering tail latency risk (CVaR$_{0.95}$) by 10.4% and achieving near-zero deadline violations. Furthermore, extensive experiments reveal that DeFRiS achieves over 3 times better performance retention as the system scales and over 8 times better stability in adversarial environments compared to the best-performing baseline.

item.title: DP-HFGL: Heterogeneous Federated Graph Learning With Differential Privacy
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Wenbo Yu, Qingqing Ye, Xun Ran, Junxu Liu, Haibo Hu
Federated Graph Learning (FGL) has garnered increasing interest thanks to its ability to harness the representational power of graphs, while its development is still impeded by privacy issues stemming from the direct upload of a participant’s local model. In this study, we address privacy concerns of FGL by Differential Privacy (DP), and devise a novel graph-level framework for Heterogeneous Federated Graph Learning with Differential Privacy (DP-HFGL). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to investigate graph-level classification tasks in federated setting, while providing rigorous DP guarantee. The primary challenges in this work stem from the intra-client feature and structure heterogeneity among graphs, inter-client statistical heterogeneity in local distribution shifts and DP-required noise injection. Specifically, these factors bring significant variance to the model gradients, leading to unstable training and utility degradation. To address these issues, DP-HFGL applies a dual-channel model to process feature and structure information separately and shares only structural information with the server, which significantly mitigates the impact of heterogeneity under noise perturbation. To further enhance the overall performance, we perform DP operations only on the shared structure knowledge to naturally reduce the norm of local updates before clipping, making local updates adaptive to the DP operations. Extensive experiments on several types of datasets, including Molecules, Proteins, Social Networks and Computer Vision, demonstrate the effectiveness of DP-HFGL in federated graph learning.

item.title: Invariant Federated Learning for Edge Intelligence: Mitigating Heterogeneity and Asynchrony via Exit Strategy and Invariant Penalty
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Ziruo Hao, Zhenhua Cui, Tao Yang, Yunjie Fang, Xin Wu, Hui Feng
This paper presents an invariant federated learning framework for resource-constrained edge intelligence. The framework first identifies and excludes low-value or aberrant clients, and then enforces model-level invariance to preserve generalization. Motivated by pretraining-based client valuation, we show that some clients may have negligible or even detrimental contributions to global aggregation under severe heterogeneity or asynchrony. Accordingly, we propose a practical exit strategy based on client utility and delay, which removes such clients from the main training loop to protect in-distribution (ID) performance. To maintain robust performance for excluded and resource-constrained clients, we introduce FedIPG (Federated Learning with Invariant Penalty for Generalization), which promotes approximate orthogonality between invariant and heterogeneous parameter components through a gradient-based penalty. We provide theoretical analysis showing that low-value client exit can improve aggregation and that FedIPG tightens an upper bound on out-of-distribution (OOD) risk without increasing communication overhead during formal training. Extensive experiments on four domain-generalization benchmarks and multiple client scales demonstrate that the combined exit + FedIPG framework improves ID accuracy, enhances OOD generalization over recent baselines, and maintains stable convergence. Visualization results further indicate that FedIPG reduces reliance on confounding features and encourages more task-relevant feature usage.
